items.title: Capturing Cultural memory with the Urban Embroidery of LAURA ORTIZ VEGA
items.summary: With a creative lexicon featuring yarn, pixels, beeswax, and spray paint, Mexican artist Laura Ortiz Vega has created a new language for herself, one that speaks to the present and the past by using traditional and conte.

items.title: Harriet Mena Hill Brings Crumbling Concrete Back To Life
items.summary: For three decades, Harriet Mena Hill has been a resident of South East London. This area is known in the art world for its schools, such as the esteemed Camberwell College of Arts.

items.title: Celestial Stance: The Art of Marigold Santos
items.summary: Marigold Santos’s spectral forms are as layered with detail as they are with metaphor. Swirling amid marbled backgrounds in a feverish dance, they serve as critical examinations of cultural injustice.

items.title: Future Relics: The Art of Morgan Sorensen
items.summary: Skeletons, tombstones, and serpents. These are just a few of the iconic images pre-v ailing throughout the works of Morgan Sorensen—all relating to the themes of struggle, sadness, pain, and death.

items.title: The Disconcertingly Honest Self-Portrait Sculptures of Monica Piloni
items.summary: The body is an obsession for Monica Piloni. Whether it’s a hollowed face in the Samieses series or the eerie dolls depicted in “Ilegais”, a majority of Monica Piloni’s sculptures confront the human form.
